title: Landing and the lane gates match their rules
goal: land, done and sync name the code/<id> branch and lane the same way, run the item's checks before an auto-merging merge request, and the pre-push, fix and publish gates refuse and accept what the lane and leak rules say; the sprint skills name set, move and reopen and the cleanup steps that an orchestrator in its own worktree can run

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?

notes: Rank 3 of the 5 active sprints. Holds the leftovers of four merged sprints: the work that makes each landing cheaper and safer, then smaller skill and doc fixes. Its three most valuable items go first: ST-tbi3rras “Sprint runs test in three tiers: narrow per task, the gate per landing, the heavy suites once at sprint end” (a worker runs only its item's checks and land stops running stress_test.py, so every later item lands faster); ST-gpodng3o “backlog.py check refuses an open item whose repro or check the live-backlog tests refuse, so a bad item fails its own push” (an item file can no longer turn main red for the next code push); and the only open S2 bug, BG-zocrzogv “red-pipeline reads a real red job older than 10 unstarted main pipelines as green, since the idle stop returns the newest finished pipeline”. ST-clsddgen “check warns of an open item whose touches name a CLI facade and no module behind it, naming the module the map gives” lands before SP-xdzgepun starts, so a facade-only touch is caught at check instead of at done. Land and done live in _tools/bl_land.py, and the items that change them name it and test_bl_land.py in their touches. The P3 items (skill wording for move and reopen, a missing planted land test, Self-Reviewed trailers on stacked commits, host-setup gates, the pipeline review on a real spool) come last.
